short: The lead ship of her class of super-dreadnoughts, she introduced 15-inch guns and oil firing to the Royal Navy battleship line.
full:
Commissioned on 22 December 1914, HMS Queen Elizabeth represented a new standard in battleship power. Seeking a decisive qualitative edge over the expanding German fleet, the Royal Navy armed her with eight 15-inch guns, vastly out-ranging contemporary vessels. She was also the first battleship designed to run entirely on oil rather than coal, increasing her top speed and reducing required manpower.

She served in the Mediterranean during the First World War, taking part in the Dardanelles campaign, and later became the flagship of the Grand Fleet, missing the Battle of Jutland due to maintenance. Rebuilt heavily between the wars, she was active in the Second World War until heavily damaged by Italian human torpedoes in Alexandria harbour in 1941, though she was subsequently repaired and served until 1948.
